mentioned.quote: Our AI Safety Framework describes the second risk category as misusing AI systems to develop hazardous biochemical weapons or otherwise use them against their original purpose.

threshold.note: Misuse matrix levels (Low risk / Risk identified / High risk, p.6) are defined by use case and need for guardrails, not by what a model could do in the biochemical domain; 'Special use case: biochemical weaponization' appears only as an example (p.5).

response.quote: Deploy AI systems only after implementing guardrails through technological and policy actions and risks have been sufficiently mitigated
response.note: Misuse matrix cell (general purpose, high need for guardrails); High risk cell reads 'Do not deploy AI systems'. Present-tense rules tied to a condition (E1), C3(b). Biochemical weaponization is the matrix's example (p.5). No threshold (gap). Surrounding prose uses 'should' (p.6).

acc_decider.quote: The board (or the risk management committee) that makes the final decisions on the matter
acc_decider.note: AI Governance; risk management working group decides which issues to raise to the board.

acc_external.note: No committed outside review. Red Teaming Challenge (p.7) is a past event; 'We will also collaborate with external experts' (p.9) commits to no review of this risk's safeguards or thresholds.

acc_unmet.quote: Withhold deployment until additional safety measures are taken
acc_unmet.note: Misuse matrix cell (Risk identified): deployment held until required safety measures are in place (E4). Measures are not named; see report.
